p. 04

The job, in 4 pages

What happens under the old siding.

Four pages, in the order the work happens. Nothing new goes on until the wall behind it has been checked.

  1. Page 1 of 4

    Measure every wall.

    Each wall, gable and opening gets measured. You get the squares and four material prices side by side, on paper.

    1/4

  2. Page 2 of 4

    Tear-off, then a sheathing check.

    Old siding comes off one wall at a time. If the sheathing under it is soft, you see it and the per-sheet price before we replace it.

    2/4

  3. Page 3 of 4

    Wrap and flashing.

    New house wrap with taped seams, and flashing bent around every window, door and deck ledger before a board goes up.

    3/4

  4. Page 4 of 4

    Courses and trim.

    Starter strip level, courses straight, corners and trim tight. Nails are swept with a magnet at the end of each day.

    4/4

p. 05

Eight jobs, scored by how much of the house they touch.

One cell is a single course. Five is the whole house.

  • Vinyl siding

    Lap and Dutch lap vinyl in dozens of colors, the lowest price per square foot we offer.

    Scope: 5 of 5 Work out my squares first

  • Fiber cement siding

    Heavy lap plank that takes knocks and holds paint well, a good fit for colonials.

    Scope: 5 of 5 See how it scored

  • Cedar clapboard

    Real cedar clapboard for older capes and Victorians, primed on all sides before it goes up.

    Scope: 4 of 5 Ask about cedar for an older house

  • Engineered wood siding

    Wood-look lap that weighs less than fiber cement and comes factory-painted in long lengths.

    Scope: 5 of 5 Check it on the price sheet

  • Repair and replacement

    Cracked, loose or rotten boards replaced and matched, from a single course to one full wall.

    Scope: 1.5 of 5 Mark the wall that needs it

  • Color consults

    Body, trim and accent colors tried on a drawing of your own house before you choose.

    Scope: 5 of 5 Book a color consult

  • Soffit and fascia

    Rotten fascia boards replaced and vented soffit added so the attic can breathe.

    Scope: 2 of 5 Have the fascia checked

  • Measure and compare visits

    We measure every wall and give you the squares and a price for each material side by side.

    Scope: 5 of 5 Book a measure visit

Five questions owners ask

Will you work with my insurance claim?

We write the scope with photos of each wall. You talk to your insurer; we answer the adjuster's questions about the work.

What if the wood under my siding is rotten?

You see it, and the per-sheet price, before anything is replaced. No new siding goes over soft wood.

How long is the house open?

One wall at a time. A wall that comes off in the morning is wrapped and flashed before the crew leaves.

My house was built before 1978.

Painted wood gets lead-safe prep: plastic on the ground, wet scraping and HEPA cleanup.

Who cleans up?

Old siding is hauled off as it comes down, and the yard is swept with a magnet at the end of each day.
